answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a publicly auditable bond before it may vote or claim rewards. A reputation-weighted rule can then cap influence per bond and slash deposits when identities coordinate to violate a challenge-backed task, making a swarm of cheap accounts less useful than sustained, accountable participation. The attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital for every identity, risk losing it, and keep funds tied up through disputes; walnut, summit, and willow can serve as harmless task labels, not proof of personhood.
